en: Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the abuses of the Spanish colonial government in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, scientifically named Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird and one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world.
The Legislative branch of the Philippine government is composed of the Senate and the House of Representatives, which work together to create national laws.
The Ifugao people carved the famous Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains of the Cordilleras over two thousand years ago using simple hand tools.
General Emilio Aguinaldo officially proclaimed Philippine independence from Spanish rule on June 12, 1898, at his ancestral home in Kawit, Cavite.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected marine sanctuary and UNESCO World Heritage site famous for its rich coral biodiversity.
Baybayin is an ancient pre-colonial Philippine writing system where each character represents a syllable, and it was traditionally written on bamboo or leaves.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was a pioneering Filipino pediatrician who invented a bamboo incubator to help provide affordable healthcare for babies in rural areas.
The Ati-Atihan festival in Kalibo, Aklan, honors the Santo Niño and features participants painting their faces with black soot while dancing in the streets.
Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, every citizen who is at least eighteen years old has the right and duty to vote in national elections.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is famous for being a volcano located on an island in the middle of Lake Taal, which fills a massive ancient crater.
The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan is famously illustrated by neighbors helping a family physically carry their entire nipa hut to a new location.
